genre: short-form podcast / interview reel (vertical, 120s or less, Shorts children)

source.measured: frame-level breakdown of 28 owner-selected premium Instagram reference reels, Oct 2026 (phase-1 refs_* analysis and DESIGN_BRIEF)
source.note: references for craft relationships only; never copy their content, logos or identities

identity: One complete micro-story lifted from a longer conversation — a hook line, the setup it needs, a turn and a payoff — delivered as a DESIGNED short-form piece. The speaker owns a composed vertical frame; a motion, typography and sound system carries the speech: framing changes on sentence turns, hero words and graphics land on the spoken word, and sound is edited to picture. Flat delivery (one static plate with subtitles and a silent mix) is the failure mode, not the safe choice.

rules.story: keep one complete micro-story: open on its strongest intelligible line, keep the setup the payoff depends on, end on the resolved line or a deliberate cliff; never splice unrelated answers into a synthetic claim; cut dead time and repairable filler word-safely
rules.hook: the first second carries a pattern interrupt (a punched-in or pushing frame, a hero title slam, a hit) and the hook line is on screen within about 1.5s; no fade from black
rules.frame: fill the vertical frame with the speaker (auto_reframe / focus_track per shot); no half-black or postage-stamp canvas; on two-person footage frame the active speaker
rules.camera: framing changes are the rhythm of a talking reel: alternate scale on jump cuts and sentence turns (references change framing every 2-5s), push slowly under an emotional hold, punch on payoffs and numbers; aim every move at the face (add_zoom with measured cx/cy) and vary strength and curve so it never reads as an automated pass
rules.typography: one designed type system: captions with a bold sans backbone and ONE accent role (keyword colour or italic serif) on 1-2 words per sentence, placed in face-free space above the platform UI band; hero words, numbers and names land as motion graphics on their spoken onset (add_motion_graphic — list_motion_templates), entrances short and graphic, exits faster than entrances
rules.motion_graphics: use the motion layer for the beats that carry the story: hook title, number counters, name/role labels, lists, social/UI cards, callouts; each graphic settles and holds still, never covers the face, and is silent unless the moment earns one library sound
rules.sound: speech is the lead; no music unless the user supplied or asked for it (never chosen by the agent); sound effects only from the approved library (list_sound_library, add_sfx storage_key='sound:<id>') and only on meaningful on-screen moments — a graphic landing (peak on the frame), a real section change or B-roll entry, the payoff, or a shown real-world action (shutter, typing, click, cash register); never on captions or ordinary cuts; about one sound every 4-5 s at most; a brief stop-down silence before a reveal
rules.transitions: hard cuts inside one take stay invisible; section turns, hook-to-body and B-roll entries may earn a whip/flash/zoom transition paired with a sound
rules.finish: one committed grade with light grain/texture; loudness mastered for social (set_master_loudness); the last frame loops cleanly into the first
